time_of_day: night (storm on 11 Sep; M&G reports flooding on Friday 12 Sep)
rain_note: Five hours of torrential rain; parts of Freetown under more than 1 m of water (Mail & Guardian/AFP, 12 Sep 2008)
summary: A storm on 11 September 2008 tore down dozens of makeshift homes in Kroo Bay and affected more than 10,000 slum dwellers, and parts of Freetown were submerged under more than 1 m of water.
evidence: More than 10,000 slum dwellers have been affected by an 11 September storm that tore down dozens of makeshift homes in Kroo Bay, one of the city's largest slums (IRIN, 16 Sep 2008)

rain_note: Heavy downpour and tropical storm extending into central Freetown
summary: A heavy downpour on Sunday 13 July 2014 (the 'last Sunday' before a 15 July column) turned parts of the highway from PK Oil Mill into fast-flowing rivers and flooded Williams Street from the blocked Samba Gutter.
evidence: Various parts of the highway, from PK Oil mill were flooded with rain water, which formed fast flowing rivers ... Williams Street may have lived to its reputation of being flooded from a blocked Samba Gutter, up to the junction with Thomas Street.

summary: On the night before 6 September 2014, Freetown had what the Sierra Leone Telegraph called its worst flooding, which closed major roads and markets.
evidence: Last night, Freetown experienced its worst flooding due to heavy rains, closing major roads and markets. (Sierra Leone Telegraph, published 6 Sep 2014)

summary: A heavy downpour on Friday 14 July 2023 flooded the main route through Regent Village toward Grafton and Freetown with debris from the hills and disrupted traffic. No casualties were reported.
evidence: Heavy downpour on Friday July 14 has caused disruption to traffic at Regent Village outside Freetown. Photos circulating on social media showed the major route to Grafton and Freetown flooded with debris from the hilly community.

time_of_day: late night 28 Jul into early hours of 29 Jul
rain_note: Heavy downpour from late 28 July into early 29 July 2023
summary: A heavy downpour overnight on 28–29 July 2023 flooded the Old Road Market Square in Waterloo (Western Area Rural) and nearly submerged stalls and shops, forcing traders to flee.
evidence: The heavy downpour which started in the late hours of Friday July 28 into the early hours of Saturday July 29 2023 has caused disruption at the Old Road Market Square in Waterloo ... the market was flooded

rain_note: Persistent torrential rains in Freetown since 1 July 2024; 20 July was the highest recorded incident
summary: Saturday 20 July 2024 was the worst day of the July 2024 rains in Freetown, with flooding in low-lying areas. NDMA said at its 30 July briefing that the July rains caused about six deaths across the city.
evidence: the highest recorded incident on Saturday, July 20, 2024, with rains causing associated impacts, including flooding in low-lying areas (Premier Media, 'Torrential Rain Causes Widespread Flooding in Freetown', seen in search result only)

summary: After a heavy downpour on 21 July 2024, a four-storey building at SS Camp near Regent collapsed at about 23:30. NDMA confirmed 1 death on 22 July, with 5 rescued and 2 children still trapped; later media put the toll at 3.
evidence: Following yesterday's heavy downpour, the National Disaster Management Agency (NDMA) received a report at approximately 11:30 PM regarding the collapse of a four-story building located at No. 132 Haja Sonnie Drive, SS Camp IMATT.

rain_note: Heavy rainfall over the weekend; SLMet heavy-rain alert for Freetown from 27 July until 15:00 on 28 July 2024
summary: Heavy rain over the weekend of 27–28 July 2024 set off a night-time landslide in Moyiba, on the eastern edge of Freetown, which buried at least six houses. No deaths were reported.
evidence: The Moyiba community in Sierra Leone has faced a severe landslide due to heavy rainfall over the past weekend, burying at least six houses under a mass of debris. (Sierraloaded, 30 Jul 2024)

summary: Early on 4 August 2024, after heavy rainfall and flooding, a fence from an abandoned house in Calaba Town collapsed onto a makeshift structure, killing a mother and three children and injuring 10 people.
evidence: A fence collapse in Alpha Tarrance, Calaba Town, has claimed the lives of four people, including a mother and three children. Ten others were injured in the incident, which occurred early this morning following heavy rainfall and flooding.

summary: Intense rain on 24 October 2024 caused severe flooding in eastern Freetown. It flooded a church and school on Texaco Old Road, destroyed 8 mud-brick homes in Lower Kuntolor (more than 150 people displaced), and collapsed a fence on Upper Melon Street that swept away two men (1 dead, 1 missing).
evidence: On Thursday, October 24, Freetown was struck by intense rainfall, resulting in severe flooding and widespread damage across several communities.

rain_note: Heavy downpour; floodwater and mud cascading from surrounding hilltops
summary: At about 18:00 on 23 July 2025, after a heavy downpour, floodwater and mud from the hills collapsed a compound fence in New England Ville onto a makeshift home. Three family members were swept away and died, and a 1-year-old was still missing.
evidence: At approximately 6:00 PM, following a heavy downpour, a section of a compound fence collapsed due to the massive flow of floodwater and mud cascading from the surrounding hilltops.

rain_note: NDMA advisory forecast 100–150 mm cumulative rainfall for 30 July–2 August 2025
summary: Heavy rain from the early hours of 31 July 2025 caused severe flooding in Kroo Bay, with water surging into homes, and flooded streets in Regent, stranding vehicles. On 1 August, erosion damage to mud homes in Dwarzack ('7 Up') was reported after hours of heavy rain, with no exact date given.
evidence: A heavy downpour in the early hours of Thursday, July 31st, 2025, has led to severe flooding in the Kroo Bay community, causing water to surge into homes and resulting in significant property damage.
